embargo

/em-BAR-go/ — rhymes with cargo · noun

Hear It

What It Means

An embargo is an official ban or restriction, often preventing trade with a country or blocking the release of certain information.

The embargo stopped all oil shipments between the two countries.

Example

After the diplomatic crisis, the nation imposed a full embargo on all trade with its neighbor, effectively shutting down the supply of imported goods.

Embargo is precise here because it captures an official governmental ban—especially on trade—with serious international consequences. 'Ban' is too generic; embargo specifically names the geopolitical trade restriction that carries legal weight.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

blockade: A blockade is a physical barrier that stops goods or people from moving — warships sealing a port, troops ringing a city. An embargo needs no ships at all: it is a legal order from a government, cutting off trade everywhere the law reaches rather than at one blocked spot.

sanction: A sanction is an official penalty meant to pressure a country into changing its behavior — a fine, frozen accounts, limits on certain sales. An embargo is one sweeping kind of pressure: instead of punishing trade, it shuts the trade down altogether.

moratorium: A moratorium is an official pause: an activity is suspended for a set time and expected to resume. An embargo is not a pause but a cutoff — a government ban on trade with a country that stands until it is deliberately lifted.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

trade: the open exchange of goods between nations

authorization: official permission allowing something to go forward

Where it sits · how wide and official the shutdown is

restriction → ban → prohibition → embargo

restriction vs. embargo: A restriction merely limits what is allowed, but an embargo is far stronger — an official government order cutting off trade almost completely.

ban vs. embargo: A ban forbids one thing outright, yet an embargo is stronger still, because an embargo is a government's official ban aimed at an entire country's trade.

prohibition vs. embargo: A prohibition is broader and more official than a simple ban, forbidding an activity wherever the law reaches, yet an embargo is stronger still — a government's prohibition aimed at an entire country's trade.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — em-: in, into, upon (Latin in-, via Spanish)

Root — bargo: bar, barrier (from Vulgar Latin barra, 'bar,' via Spanish embargar, 'to seize, impede')

Put it together: Em- ('in, upon') + bargo ('bar, barrier,' from Vulgar Latin barra via Spanish embargar): an embargo literally puts a bar in the way — an official barrier set up by a government to block trade or hold back information.

Use the root in a new word: barrier: The crowd pressed against the barrier long before the parade's first float appeared.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal

Embargo is the formal, official term for governmental trade restrictions or information bans—use it when discussing nations or official policy. For a simple prohibition, 'ban' works fine.
